## FIRST RECURRENCE OF CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)
Discontinue implicated antibiotic(s). Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic
therapy is still needed. Avoid antiperistaltic agents (narcotics, loperamide,
etc.). Avoid antacid therapy without clear indication. If diarrhea has improved
or resolved prior to starting C. difficile treatment, consider re-assessing the
diagnosis before initiating therapy. C. difficile infection usually responds to
antimicrobial therapy. If symptoms do not respond to appropriate antimicrobial
therapy, re-consider the diagnosis.
## First Recurrence CDI: *The REGIMEN should be different from initial treatment.*
## Inpatient

[Vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h for 10 days [M]](psjzid-vancomycin-125mg-po-q6h-x10days-cdiff)
< OR >
[Vancomycin Extended-Pulse Taper Regimen [M]](psjzid-vancomycin-taper-and-pulse-dosing)
(Vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h for 10 days, then taper and pulse with 125 mg po q12h
for 7 days, then 125mg po qday for 7 days, then 125mg every other day for 6
weeks)
< OR >
[Fidaxomicin 200 mg po q12h for 10 days [M]](psjzid-fidaxomicin-200mg-q12h-10d)
< OR >
[Fidaxomicin Extended-Pulse Regimen [M]](psjzid-fidaxomicin-extended-pulse-regimen)
(Fidaxomicin 200mg po bid x5days, then 200mg every other day x 20days)
